experiments.title: Experiment 015: Multimodal Measurement Selection
experiments.summary: Five candidate sensing modalities were investigated under a measurement budget of three.

setup.seeds: Multiple experimental seeds (number to be confirmed)

tables.title: Preliminary mean results across experimental seeds

experiments.interpretation: These results demonstrate condition-dependent performance rather than universal adaptive superiority. In the aggregate table, the random strategy obtains the highest unknown-condition detection metric; under held-out drift the adaptive strategy obtains the highest value, while under held-out precipitation it obtains the lowest.
methodNotes: Measurement budget of three out of five candidate modalities.
Held-out conditions were not seen during strategy design (protocol to be confirmed).
The quantity reported in the held-out table is assumed to be the same detection metric expressed as a percentage; this must be confirmed.
limitations: Number of seeds and per-seed variance not yet reported; no confidence intervals.
Synthetic simulation environment; no physical instrument data.
Metric definition and direction (higher-is-better) pending confirmation.

experiments.title: Experiment 015g: Reference-Based Strategies
experiments.summary: Comparison of strategies that make use of a reference observation.

setup.measurementBudget: To be confirmed — the all-five reference strategy uses every modality, so budgets are not directly comparable.

experiments.interpretation: In this configuration the fixed reference strategy outperforms the adaptive reference strategy. The all-five reference strategy obtains the highest value but, by using all five modalities, likely operates under a larger measurement budget; it should be treated as an upper reference rather than a like-for-like competitor.
methodNotes: Reference strategies are compared on the unknown-condition detection metric only; false positive rates to be reported.
limitations: Budget comparability between strategies must be confirmed.

experiments.title: Experiment 015h: Hybrid Reference-First Strategy
experiments.summary: A hybrid strategy that acquires a reference observation first and then selects remaining measurements.
experiments.interpretation: The hybrid reference-first strategy reports higher detection values than the strategies in Experiment 015 at a similar false positive rate. Whether this reflects the strategy itself or differences in budget, reference access, or protocol has not yet been established.
methodNotes: Precipitation and drift values are reported here on a 0–1 scale; Experiment 015 held-out values are reported in percent. Confirm that these are the same metric before comparing them directly.
limitations: Budget comparability with Experiment 015 must be confirmed.
Ablations (reference-only, reference + fixed) not yet reported.
